title: Companion Warm-Pool Proxy & Tenant Stowage — PRD sketch
body:
Context:
This is a sketch for a complementary mechanism to existing Dedicated autoscaling and burst strategies: a lightweight "companion" warm-pool proxy that mediates short-lived tenant bursts and a tenant "stowage" concept to temporally relocate low-priority work into cheap, pre-warmed slots. The goal is to reduce cold-start latencies for bursty tenants while preserving strong tenant isolation and predictable SLOs for reserved capacity customers.

Motivation / Problem statement:
- Many customers purchase reserved capacity but still have microburst patterns (e.g., >10s of high QPS for <60s). We need to avoid frequent cold starts while keeping isolation and billing clarity.
- Hard prewarmed pools (hot pools) are expensive to keep active for every tenant.
- Existing burst lanes either degrade latency or risk cross-tenant interference when oversubscription occurs.

High level concept:
1) Companion Warm-Pool Proxy (CWP): a lightweight proxy service that sits between tenant routing and the Dedicated serving pool. It maintains short-lived, soft-warmed model worker slots that are "paired" with a customer's reserved capacity but live in a separate runtime plane.
   - Soft-warmed: model weights loaded with quantization-ready kernels but without persistent KV cache for ongoing sessions.
   - Time-to-serve target: <150ms additional overhead for the first token for microbursts <90s.
   - CWP enforces per-tenant burst budgets and observable headroom signals to the autoscaler.

2) Tenant Stowage: when Dedicated pools are at risk of contention, we offer a graceful stowage lane for background/low-priority requests. These requests are routed to ephemeral, cheaper warm slots that accept best-effort quality and can be throttled or answered with shorter contexts.
   - Use cases: backfill reranking, non-interactive embeddings, batched fine-tuning preprocessing jobs, low-priority analytics transforms.

Core behaviors and controls:
- Admission policy: each tenant gets a companion config: {companion-size, burst-window, stowage-eligibility}. Admins can opt-in per SKU.
- Budgeting: companions consume a burst-credit ledger (time-decay credits). Credits refill with reserved capacity usage and monthly top-ups for committed customers.
- Degradation ladder: primary serving (reserved pools) -> CWP fast-warm path -> stowage -> fallback to hosted variants (if configured).
- Isolation guarantees: CWP instances are single-tenant processes where feasible; where multi-tenant is used, strict cgroups and network shaping apply. Memory and GPU memory caps enforce per-instance isolation.

Autoscaling integration:
- Observability hooks: CWP exposes headroom, warm-slot utilization, recent first-token latencies as metrics. The dedicated autoscaler consumes these to decide on prewarm actions in the main pool.
- Predictive prewarm: use short-term windows (5–30m) derived from CWP burst traces to request additional reserved capacity from the capacity broker (soft warm) rather than on-demand cold starts.
- Soft failover: if autoscaler cannot supply more reserved slots, CWP scales up internal warm pool (within budget) and signals degraded latency band to customers.

Cost & billing model proposals:
- Companion surcharge: small % fee on top of reserved capacity for each tenant using companion warm pool (tiered by companion-size).
- Stowage discount band: stowage requests billed at a discounted per-token rate but with weaker SLOs (documented).
- Burst credits visible in console and line-itemed on invoices.

Operational considerations / runbook notes:
- On sustained high utilization (>5m over threshold), CWP should automatically promote warm slots to persistent reserved workers via the capacity broker to avoid repeated conversions.
- Eviction policy: least-recently-used companions trimmed first; stowage requests throttled according to bucket token refill.
- Incident signals: abnormal first-token latencies or repeated promotion failures should trigger an ops page and create a high-severity ticket assigned to dedicated-capacity-oncall.

Security & compliance:
- Companion processes must respect same KMS/HSM flows and audit logging as reserved pools.
- Stowage lanes should be opt-in for customers with regulated data; by default, tenant-stowage disallowed for data-classified workloads unless explicitly approved.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How much of the CWP must be single-tenant to maintain acceptable isolation vs cost? (estimate: small tenants -> multi-tenant; enterprise -> single-tenant).
- Granularity of credit refill: per-hour vs per-minute. Faster refill gives better UX but makes billing more complex.
- Interaction with preemption: when capacity is tight, should companions be preemptible if higher-tier tenants need it? Likely yes, but need explicit SLA contracts.

Technical notes / prototype plan:
- Phase 0: implement a proxy shim that fronts an existing warm pool implementation; collect burst telemetry for 30 customers. Instrument first-token time, cold-start count, and stowage acceptance rate.
- Phase 1: add companion ledger and simple prewarm strategy (threshold-based) in autoscaler. Expose UI in console to configure companion-size and stowage flags.
- Phase 2: upgrade to predictive prewarm using 1-hour sequence models; integrate cross-tenant headroom broker.

Metrics to validate success (initial):
- Reduction in 1st-token latency p95 for microburst windows by >=40% compared to baseline without CWP.
- Reduction in cold-start rate per tenant by >=70% during measured burst events.
- Cost delta: companions should not increase unit cost by more than 8% for committed customers (goal).

UI / Console controls (sketch):
- Companion config panel: enable/disable, companion-size slider, burst window selector, stowage toggle.
- Burst ledger viewer: live credits, burn rate, refill projections.
- Observability tab: headroom timeline, warm-slot utilization, promoted-slot events.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: companions encourage customers to rely on microbursts instead of right-sizing commitments -> Mitigation: tiered pricing + visible cost projection that discourages abuse.
- Risk: cross-tenant leakage in multi-tenant companion mode -> Mitigation: strong OS-level isolation, strict quotas, telemetry-backed anomaly detection.

Action items / next steps:
- [Leah] prototype proxy shim and gather burst telemetry (2 weeks).
- [Marco] design companion-ledger schema and proposed billing entries (1 week).
- [Aisha] security review for stowage lane (1 week).
- [Omar] run small pilot with 3 committed customers and report early metrics (4 weeks).

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally a rough sketch — looking for feedback on: 1) whether companion warm pool is a product distinction (vs just more prewarming), 2) acceptable budget/credit models, and 3) whether stowage introduces unacceptable compliance surface area.
